p: (a To know whether I complain without just cause.
swallowed up: My grief is so great that I lack words to express it.
set themselves in array against me: Which declares that he was not only afflicted in body, but wounded in conscience, which is the greatest battle that the faithful can have.
wild ass bray when he hath: Do you think that I cry without cause, seeing the brute beasts do not complain when they have what they want.

unsavoury be eaten without salt: Can a man's taste delight in that, which has no savour? meaning that no one takes pleasure in affliction seeing they cannot do away with things that are unsavoury to the mouth.
request: In this he sins double, both in wishing through impatience to die, and also in desiring of God a thing which was not agreeable to his will.
for I have not concealed the: That is, let me die at once before I come to distrust God's promise through my impatience.
end: He fears lest he should be brought to inconveniences, if his sorrows should continue.
help in me: Have I not sought to help myself as much as was possible?

brook: He compares friends who do not comfort us in our misery to a brook which in summer when we need water is dry, in winter is hard frozen and in the time of rain when we have no need overflows with water.
looked: They who pass by it to go into the hot countries of Arabia, think to find water there to quench their thirst but they are deceived.
nothing: That is, like this brook which deceives them who think to have water there in their need, as I looked for consolation from you.
substance: He touches the worldlings who for need will give part of their goods, and much more these men, who would not give him comfortable words.
hold my tongue: Show me where I have erred, and I will confess my sin.
forcible are right words: He who has a good conscience does not shrink at the sharp words or reasonings of others, unless they are able to persuade him by reason.
words: Do you object to my words because I would be thought to speak foolishly, and am now in misery?
look upon me: Consider whether I speak as one who is driven to this impatience through sorrow, or as a hypocrite as you condemn me.
